methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a Norfolk native directly address the technology gap through grassroots peer learning, signaling potential for distributed AI fluency outside traditional tech hubs if this community-driven model scales.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI capability development in a non-metro region, potentially creating a distributed node of expertise if graduates stay local rather than migrate to NoVA.

signals.title: Meta, Google invest in skilled worker training to build Virginia data centers - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Meta and Google's data center workforce training initiatives suggest platform-led skill development that may create broad but shallow AI adoption—workers trained for operations rather than development, reinforcing concentrated innovation elsewhere.

signals.title: Inside the AI-powered system sorting Hampton Roads' trash - 13newsnow.com
signals.signal_reading: AI-powered waste sorting represents turnkey platform deployment requiring minimal local AI expertise—a signal of shallow, automated adoption that doesn't build regional capability to develop AI solutions independently.

signals.title: Second Major Virginia Data Center Project Dies, Raising AI Site Selection Stakes - Data Center Knowledge
signals.signal_reading: Failed data center projects in NoVA amid rising competition signal that even in Virginia's deepest AI infrastructure hub, concentrated advantage faces pressure—though rejection also shows communities gaining agency over extractive vs. generative tech development.
